facts.statement: Unaysaurus was discovered in 1998 in the Paleorrota geopark in southern Brazil and officially announced on December 3, 2004.
facts.quote: Discovered in southern Brazil, in the geopark of Paleorrota, in 1998, and announced in a press conference on Thursday, December 3, 2004

facts.statement: The genus name Unaysaurus is derived from the Tupi word for 'black water', referring to the Agua Negra region where fossils were found.
facts.quote: The generic name, "Unaysaurus", comes from the word (u-na-hee), meaning "black water" in the local Tupi language

facts.statement: The species name tolentinoi honors Tolentino Marafiga, the person who found the fossils in 1998.
facts.quote: The specific name, "tolentinoi" honors Tolentino Marafiga, who discovered the fossils by the side of a road in 1998

facts.statement: Unaysaurus tolentinoi was described as a new genus and species in 2004 by Leal, Azevodo, Kellner, and da Rosa.
facts.quote: In 2004, Luciano A. Leal, Sergio A. K. Azevodo, Alexander W. A. Kellner, and Átila A. S. da Rosa described Unaysaurus tolentinoi as a new genus and species

facts.statement: The fossil material includes an almost complete skull with a lower jaw and a partial skeleton where many bones remain connected in their natural positions.
facts.quote: They consist of an almost complete skull, including a lower jaw, and partial skeleton with many of the bones still connected to each other in their natural positions

facts.statement: Unaysaurus was a small dinosaur measuring 2.5 meters in length, 70 to 80 centimeters in height, and weighing approximately 70 kilograms.
facts.quote: It was only 2.5 m long, 70 to 80 cm tall, and weighed about 70 kg

facts.statement: Unaysaurus was a bipedal dinosaur that walked on two legs, similar to most early dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Like most early dinosaurs, Unaysaurus was relatively small, and walked on two legs

facts.statement: A juvenile specimen of Unaysaurus associated with the holotype was described in 2023 by Müller and colleagues.
facts.quote: In 2023, Müller and colleagues described the remains of a juvenile specimen of Unaysaurus that was found associated with the holotype

facts.statement: Unaysaurus lived during the late Triassic period, specifically between 225 and 200 million years ago in the Carnian or Norian ages.
facts.quote: Unaysaurus lived between about 225 to 200 million years ago, in the Carnian or Norian age of the late Triassic period

facts.statement: Unaysaurus inhabited southern Brazil, a region that was connected to northwest Africa during the Triassic.
facts.quote: It was found in the south of Brazil, which at the time was connected to northwest Africa

facts.statement: During the time Unaysaurus lived, the Earth was dominated by the supercontinent Pangaea, which was beginning to split into Laurasia and Gondwana.
facts.quote: The whole world was united into the great supercontinent of Pangaea, which was just starting to divide into Laurasia in the north, and Gondwana in the south

facts.statement: Unaysaurus is classified as a herbivorous sauropodomorph dinosaur belonging to the family Unaysauridae.
facts.quote: Unaysaurus is a genus of herbivorous unaysaurid sauropodomorph dinosaur

facts.statement: When first described, Unaysaurus was initially classified within the family Plateosauridae.
facts.quote: Upon its description, Unaysaurus was assigned to the Plateosauridae

facts.statement: In 2018, Unaysaurus was reclassified into the new clade Unaysauridae, grouping it with Macrocollum and Jaklapallisaurus.
facts.quote: However, in 2018, Unaysaurus was found to belong to the newly erected clade Unaysauridae, alongside Macrocollum and Jaklapallisaurus

facts.statement: Research indicated that the closest relative of Unaysaurus was Plateosaurus, a species that lived approximately 210 million years ago in Germany.
facts.quote: the closest relative of Unaysaurus was, counter intuitively, not from South America, but rather Plateosaurus, which lived about 210 million years ago in Germany

facts.statement: The relationship between Unaysaurus and plateosaurids in Germany suggests that species could easily spread across the supercontinent Pangaea.
facts.quote: It is closely related to plateosaurid dinosaurs found in Germany, which indicates that it was relatively easy for species to spread across the giant landmass of the time, the supercontinent of Pangaea

facts.statement: The Caturrita Formation, where Unaysaurus fossils were found, contains a wide variety of fauna and is part of the Santa Maria 2 Sequence.
facts.quote: The Caturrita Formation has uncovered a wide variety of fauna, although the formation is also referred to as the upper portion of the Santa Maria 2 Sequence

facts.statement: Unaysaurus is recognized as one of the oldest known dinosaurs.
facts.quote: It is one of the oldest dinosaurs known

rejected.statement: Unaysaurus represents one of the most complete dinosaur skeletons, including a complete skull, ever recovered in Brazil.
rejected.quote: It is one of the most complete dinosaur skeletons (including complete skull) ever recovered in Brazil
